content: 1. The efficacy of azithromycin as a single 1g dose for the treatment of uncomplicated gonorrhea was evaluated in a study published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2004. The study demonstrated its effectiveness in managing this condition. 2. A randomized controlled trial compared azithromycin with doxycycline/ciprofloxacin for the syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in resource-limited settings. The findings, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, highlighted patient values, preferences, acceptability, and cost considerations in STI management. 3. An audit of the use of benzathine penicillin for early infectious syphilis, including post-treatment serology and partner notification, was conducted. The results, published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2006, emphasized the importance of comprehensive management strategies for syphilis. 4. A study on the acceptability and compliance of daily procaine penicillin injections for outpatient syphilis treatment was published in the journal Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 1997. The research focused on patient adherence to this treatment regimen. 5. An audit of early syphilis management at North Manchester General Hospital, published in 2004, provided insights into clinical practices and outcomes for syphilis treatment. 6. A systematic review on the prevalence and utilization of healthcare services for reproductive tract infections and sexually transmitted infections in India was published in the Indian Journal of Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2015. The review highlighted gaps in healthcare access and service delivery. 7. The Gonococcal Antimicrobial Surveillance Programme (GASP) provided data on antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae from 2009 to 2013. The findings, reported in the Global STI Surveillance Report, revealed high rates of quinolone resistance, increasing resistance to azithromycin, and elevated ceftriaxone minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) in gonorrhea isolates. 8. Treatment failures with ceftriaxone and cefixime were documented in several countries, emphasizing the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance in gonorrhea management. These findings were supported by studies conducted in lowand middle-income countries. 9. The World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae highlighted the emergence of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant strains. Since 2009, 46 countries have reported decreased susceptibility to extended-spectrum cephalosporins, with treatment failures documented in multiple regions. 10. Azithromycin resistance was reported in 17 out of 42 countries in 2012-2013, with resistance rates exceeding 5% in some regions. The European Region accounted for the majority of reports, with some countries documenting resistance rates over 10%. 11. Ciprofloxacin resistance was widespread, with nearly all reporting countries documenting resistance rates above 20%. Twelve countries, primarily in Asia, reported resistance rates exceeding 90%, underscoring the limited utility of quinolones in gonorrhea treatment. 12. High-level ceftriaxone resistance was reported in strains from Japan, France, Spain, and Australia. These strains exhibited novel genetic mutations contributing to resistance, as documented in studies published in leading microbiology and antimicrobial journals. 13. Verified treatment failures with cefixime were reported in Norway, England, France, Austria, and South Africa. These failures were associated with high-level resistance and novel genetic mutations in Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains. 14. The WHO emphasized the need for global surveillance and updated treatment guidelines to address the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance in gonorrhea. Collaborative efforts are required to ensure effective treatment options remain available.
